what_this_is: The Workshop rows for tools/guard-ai-spending: an AI's own spending kept inside the budget its person set (reserve before paying, check just before paying, record after paying, reset each day) and the rails that may pay. Each row reaches the person's own spend records through the run's records door. None can raise a limit or turn a budget on.

payload.label: Reserve a spend within budget
payload.job: Before my AI spends money, check the spend against my budget and work out the reservation, or refuse it
payload.description: Checks one spend (whole cents) against the person's spend authority, read from their records: it must be turned on and active, and stay inside the daily limit and the per-spend limit. Answers approved and the reason, and the check and the reservation the spend carries as `write` for the caller's AI to put in a store (this tool keeps nothing); a refused spend is answered too, with its reason. A zero-cost operation is checked and fenced without using the budget. The same idempotency key while its reservation is current answers the first reservation again and nothing to write, and counts nothing twice. No authority record means every positive spend is refused. The limits are read from the person's own records, never taken from the caller.

spend_authority_ref.description: The person's spend authority to spend from, like "spend-authority:research"

operation_ref.description: What the money is for, like "operation:buy-a-report"

rail_ref.description: The rail that will pay, like "payment-rail:x402"

spender_id.description: Which AI or worker is spending

idempotency_key.description: The same key for the same spend sent again

ttl_seconds.description: How long the reservation stays current (300 when left out)

stored.description: What this run reads of the person's own things, read by the caller from where the person keeps them (the engine keeps none) and given here: records: [{id, type, value}] of spend-authority, spend-budget-reservation, as this row's `stored` lists. What is not given is not there.

write.description: The records for the caller's AI to put in a store, each { id, type, value, expected }: expected is the record as this run read it (null for a new one), so a store refuses the write when it moved. Empty when nothing changes.

provenance.source: bitfield-packages packages/agent-wallet (do-work/decide-budget.mjs and action:budget-gate), ported to the records door

payload.label: May this spend go ahead
payload.job: Just before my AI pays, check that the spend still holds its one current budget reservation
payload.description: Reads the latest budget check and the reservation for one operation and answers available only when the check approved this operation, idempotency key and spend authority, has not expired, and exactly one current reservation matches it. Answers the reason, the reserved amount in whole cents and the reservation's fencing token. It changes nothing.

stored.description: What this run reads of the person's own things, read by the caller from where the person keeps them (the engine keeps none) and given here: records: [{id, type, value}] of spend-budget-check, spend-budget-reservation, as this row's `stored` lists. What is not given is not there.

provenance.source: bitfield-packages packages/agent-wallet read-data/read-agent-budget-authority.ts, ported to the records door

payload.label: Record a spend
payload.job: After my AI has paid, work out the new today's and all-time totals and the payment record
payload.description: Adds one paid spend (whole cents) to the spend authority's total for today and for all time, read from the person's records, and answers the new totals and the payment record as `write` for the caller's AI to put in a store (this tool keeps nothing; the authority write is conditional on the totals as read). One payment is added once: sending the same payment_ref again (the operation_ref when left out) answers the record already kept and nothing to write. It records what was paid; it never authorizes a spend.

payment_ref.description: The rail's own reference for this payment

facilitator_response.description: What the rail answered, kept with the payment

stored.description: What this run reads of the person's own things, read by the caller from where the person keeps them (the engine keeps none) and given here: records: [{id, type, value}] of spend-authority, spend-payment, as this row's `stored` lists. What is not given is not there.

write.description: The records for the caller's AI to put in a store, each { id, type, value, expected }: expected is the record as this run read it (null for a new one), so a store refuses the write when it moved. Empty when nothing changes.

payload.label: Reset today's spend
payload.job: When a new day starts (UTC), work out setting my AI's spend today back to zero
payload.description: Answers the spend authority's total for today set back to zero the first time it runs on a new UTC day, and that day, as `write` for the caller's AI to put in a store (this tool keeps nothing); every later run the same day answers nothing to write. Answers whether it reset, the day and today's total. Meant to run on a schedule each day.

payload.label: Read spend rails
payload.job: See which ways my AI may pay (card, bank, x402 and others) and which rail rows are refused
payload.description: Reads the rails shipped with this tool and the person's own payment-rail records (a person's row replaces a shipped row of the same id). Answers each valid rail's id, label, whether it is turned on, the spend authority it spends from, the name of the credential it settles with and its settlement tool, and the rows refused because they do not go through the budget reservation and the spend record. It never shows a key.

stored.description: What this run reads of the person's own things, read by the caller from where the person keeps them (the engine keeps none) and given here: records: [{id, type, value}] of payment-rail, as this row's `stored` lists. What is not given is not there.
